name: Linzumi
long_description:
Linzumi is the chat your engineering team uses to direct dozens of AI coding agents.

Kick off work, review it, ship it. All from chat.

See every agent's work. Unblock the agents that need you from your laptop, your phone, the coffee line. Your teammates see it too.

Every decision your team makes compiles into a source of truth - what to build, why it changed, how your agents should act. That same source generates new work and verifies completed work.

Deliberative alignment, repurposed from aligning LLMs to aligning companies.
one_liner: Team chat to command all your company's coding agents

launches.title: Linzumi: team chat for directing AI coding agents
launches.tagline: Team chat for directing dozens of AI coding agents
launches.body:
# Hi everyone, I'm Sean, and I’m launching Linzumi today

**Linzumi is the team chat your engineering team uses to direct dozens of AI coding agents at once.** Kick off work, review it, ship it: all from chat. Try it at <https://linzumi.com>.

> For a limited time, every team chat account also gets free daily access to state of the art open-weights intelligence, GLM 5.2 at high speed, through our partnership with [Wafer.ai](http://Wafer.ai).

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EM53ACaIHyg>

## The problem

The bottleneck in software has moved. Execution is basically free now: AI agents can write, test, and ship code 24/7. _The new constraint is human decisions and verification_. Whoever surfaces the right decision to the right person at the right moment unlocks 10x throughput. Whoever doesn't watches their agent fleet stall.

If you've ever tried to keep three coding agents productive at once, you know the feeling. You jump between PR tabs, miss approvals buried in Slack, and find one agent has sat idle for 20 minutes waiting on a one-line decision. It's a fascinating moment to be building software: vastly easier and vastly harder at the same time.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=103435&key=user_uploads/19683/9019e12e-5088-4b41-9321-28a417dade5a)

## How Linzumi works

Connect your machine, kick off work in chat, and review what every agent is doing from your laptop, your phone, or the coffee line. Works with Codex today, Claude Code coming soon. Your teammates see it all too: agent work is no longer buried in invisible terminals.

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AQP5tQGZ9Jc>

But the real unlock is underneath. As your team works, Linzumi keeps every decision close to the work itself: what to build, why it changed, who approved it, and what the agents should do next. The decision inbox surfaces only the calls that need a human, so instead of reconstructing context from terminals, PRs, chats, and memory, your team has one shared place to steer the whole fleet.

_Continuous Context Compilation_

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TNJbWKYiDyc>

## Backstory

I'm a 3x YC founder. Before Linzumi I was at OpenAI on post-training and alignment research, where I worked on systems for making models follow written specs and produce more reliable reasoning. Working with coding agents on my own projects showed me the same kind of coordination problem at the team level: the agents could execute, but the bottleneck was deciding what should happen next and checking whether the result matched intent.

The mission now is to make everyone the CEO of their own 1,000-agent company: able to direct more work, make better decisions, and become the best version of themselves as a builder.

When you combine that shared context with calibrated decisions, even the smallest form factor can do surprising amounts of work, like shipping a customer feature from your phone on the way to the meeting.

_Hands-free work_

<https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pmqf3kwuOqI>

## What we're asking for

If you run AI coding agents (or want to), try Linzumi at <https://linzumi.com>. It's free to get started and we'd love your feedback.

We're especially looking for:

• Engineering teams running multiple coding agents who want to scale to dozens (honestly, thousands by end of year)

• Founders who feel like the bottleneck in their own dev cycle

• Anyone curious about better human-agent coordination for company-scale work

DM me on X (@sgrove) or email [sean@linzumi.com](mailto:sean@linzumi.com). I read every reply.
